prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro: urban railway (peak/off-peak/engineering-hour; underground/surface); Communications-Based Train Control (CBTC): separation, movement authority (MA), regulation. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (LTC: monitors Lantern; picks holding/skip-stop/turnback/run-through, executed only if interlocking and CBTC agree; no vital intervention; produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice; applies station holds via dispatch controls into CBTC departure logic without changing route locking; verifies revised timetable). Revenue Train Operator (sees MA, speed, location confidence; acknowledges to Atlas; repeats back Voice Dispatch Console instructions; reports condition/hazards). Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple (uses Maintenance Diagnostic Server, alias Quarry: health/trends; records station interface faults, rejected commands, inconsistent indications; Maple verifies track clearance before route restore). Cyber Security Officer (reviews certificate changes, access, auth failures; reviews passenger-info/dispatch workstation access on commissioning/change). Local station staff: indications from validated CBTC states (normal, held train, door interlock fault, radio degraded, emergency stop, evacuation support). Elements: Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern (regulation, alarms; shows route/points/occupancy separately; workstation-identical station/platform identifiers; coordinates timetable deviation, platform closure, crowding before passenger release; sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas). North District Zone Controller, alias Marble; South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid: send MA to Atlas; overlap/flank protection; point correspondence loss shortens MA; axle counter conflict restrictive; handover checks. Marble suppresses departure on unsafe doors. East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon (Axle Counter Reset Request), West Junction Interlocking (Route Release Exception List): final vital authority. Platform Screen Door Controller sends Platform Door Status Snapshot to CBTC. Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel: ATP, doors; modes initialization, protected manual, ATO, fallback, cutout; Brake Curve Checksum Log; reports door enable side, berth identity, departure readiness. Dual Channel Odometer. Train Radio Modem via Wayside Radio Access Network; uses Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack (from Cryptographic Key Management Appliance) before renewed secure sessions. Saffron (alias, full name unstated): maintains station-interface message paths across coverage transitions. Safety Data Communication Network: safety station messages separate from nonvital passenger info. Voice Dispatch Console: shows calling identity, platform, hold reason; positive confirm/cancel states. Service Timetable Server: planned context; approved-workflow

New part:
S150: During degraded operation, the CBTC system favours restrictive platform states and requires explicit controller action before restoring automatic departure support at the affected station.
S151: Diagnostics and maintenance for the Greenvale Metro communications-based train control system are organised around prompt event collection, controlled remote access, and traceable engineering decisions.
S152: Each safety-related part records time-stamped events for state changes, command acceptance, rejected commands, communication loss, and local protective actions.
S153: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server receives event streams from fixed and onboard equipment through monitored interfaces that do not allow maintenance traffic to alter train movement authority.
S154: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server uses the checksum log to compare stored braking data identifiers against the expected maintenance baseline for the affected train.
S155: Remote diagnostic sessions are initiated by a Signal Maintenance Engineer and are limited to read-only observation unless an approved maintenance window authorises a specific intervention.
S156: The Cyber Security Officer reviews privileged diagnostic access logs and confirms that remote connections use current credentials and approved encryption settings.
S157: The Line Traffic Controller receives the Route Release Exception List during incident triage and uses it to check whether a release anomaly could affect service recovery decisions.
S158: Marble records controller health, interface state, and fallback mode transitions in a form that can be correlated with adjacent wayside and operations records.
S159: The South District Zone Controller maintains comparable diagnostic coverage so that boundary events can be reviewed without relying on a single source of evidence.
S160: The East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking report route command histories, point detection changes, and protective lock status to support failure localisation.
S161: The Atlas Onboard Controller stores onboard fault codes, movement authority acceptance records, propulsion cutback requests, and train interface exceptions for later retrieval.
S162: The Dual Channel Odometer provides distance and speed plausibility information that is retained with trainborne diagnostic records after any odometry disagreement.
S163: The Train Radio Modem records bearer loss, reconnection timing, signal quality indicators, and message retry counts needed to distinguish radio coverage issues from equipment faults.
S164: The Wayside Radio Access Network and Safety Data Communication Network provide communication performance records that are compared with controller logs during network-related investigations.
S165: The Metro Operations Control System displays selected fault summaries to the Line Traffic Controller but does not expose detailed maintenance commands at the traffic control workstation.
S166: A Revenue Train Operator reports observed cab indications, train handling effects, and passenger service impacts using the operational reporting channel defined for degraded service.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
